issues: Scrambled/merged list markers: several lettered items are concatenated (e.g., "andc.", "danc.", "advokat,f.", "h." on same line), which breaks list structure required for downstream splitting.
Numbering/line-break issue in Article 1: item 20 and 21 are merged into one paragraph and item 21 marker is not on its own line; item 17 lacks the ending punctuation/line break before item 18.
Numbering/structure issue in Article 7: paragraph marker "(2)" is merged into the end of item d. instead of being a separate paragraph/line.
Minor meaning drift/terminology: "repatriation" for "pemulangan" is potentially misleading in domestic context; better rendered as "return" (pemulangan) while keeping meaning consistent.

Broken list/numbering structure in Article 7: item (2) is not formatted consistently as a numbered list item and is merged into the same paragraph block, unlike the original which has (2) as a separate numbered item.

Minor meaning drift in Article 7(2): Indonesian 'diatur dengan Peraturan Bupati' is a complete clause; translation ends with a semicolon and should end as a sentence (period) to match legal drafting and avoid downstream parsing issues.

Scrambled/merged list markers in multiple places: missing spaces/newlines cause items to run together (e.g., 'andf.', 'andh.', 'services for:a.', 'may:a.', 'andb.'). This breaks list structure required for downstream splitting.
Article 17 numbering structure is broken: paragraph (2) is merged into paragraph (1) on the same line, and lettered subitems are not clearly separated from the lead-in.
Minor meaning drift/terminology: 'pemulangan' is translated as 'repatriation' (can imply cross-border return); a more neutral 'return' better matches the Indonesian in this local context.

Broken/scrambled list structure in Article 20: original has inline markers “a.” and “b.” on the same line; translation split them into separate lines and added a blank line, changing list-item boundary structure used for downstream splitting.

Minor meaning drift in Article 12(2): Indonesian states the houses “guarantee in the implementation of” the listed services; translation renders as “shall guarantee the implementation of ... services” (acceptable), but to stay closer to source phrasing, adjust to “shall guarantee, in the implementation of services, ...”.

Scrambled list/numbering structure in Article 8: original uses lettered items (Huruf a, b, c) but translation uses 'Point a/b/c' as plain text instead of preserving the list markers as separate items in the same order.

Broken list/numbering structure in Article 8: original uses in-line markers 'Huruf a/b/c' (letter a/b/c) but translation converts them to a., b., c. list items, which changes the marker format required for downstream boundary matching.
